idiom_name: one table per scope (name -> symbol map plus enclosing-scope link) with a define pass and a resolve pass
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: represent each scope explicitly as an object holding a map from name to symbol plus a link to the enclosing scope (or keep a stack of open scopes while walking the tree). Run a definition pass that inserts every declaration into the scope that owns it - applying the language's hoisting and declaration-order rules, rejecting duplicates within a scope while allowing shadowing across scopes - then a resolution pass that walks each identifier use from the innermost scope outward, takes the first match, stores the result on the use site as a scope distance, de Bruijn index or direct symbol reference, and reports names that resolve nowhere. Keep a separate table per namespace where the language distinguishes terms, types, macros and labels; decide symbol lifetime deliberately (later phases address symbols by identity, so they must outlive the pass); and keep one resolver instance per compilation so no state leaks between inputs.
pitfalls: Resolving on the fly while parsing: forward references and mutually recursive declarations cannot be handled without a definition pass, and the parser grows a second responsibility.
One scope object reused for a whole compilation (or shared between threads): results then depend on the previous input.
Freeing scopes as soon as they close while later phases still hold pointers to the symbols inside them.

Wrong move: give every syntactic block its own table in a language whose declarations hoist to the enclosing function (JavaScript var) -> failure: names still visible outside the block are reported undeclared or treated as distinct shadowed bindings, and duplicate var declarations in sibling blocks go undetected -> instead: model the language's real scope lattice - var binds at the function scope, let/const at the block - as two interleaved scope kinds, not one table per brace.

Wrong move: assume every lexically nested scope participates in lookup -> failure: a Python class body executes in its own table but is not an enclosing scope for nested functions, so a method name that should reach a module global instead resolves through the class table and fails -> instead: mark which scope kinds are transparent to lookup (class bodies and similar non-enclosing scopes) and skip them in the walk.

Wrong move: cache resolutions as source positions in an editor-backed resolver -> failure: an edit above the use shifts coordinates and go-to-definition silently binds to the wrong declaration -> instead: key stored bindings to AST or symbol nodes owned by the parse and re-run resolution when the tree is rebuilt, never trusting stale coordinates.
